sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Nashville?
sections.html:
Two Metro offices split the work. The Assessor of Property decides what your house is worth for tax purposes, and the Office of the Metropolitan Trustee mails the bill and accepts payment.

Nashville and Davidson County operate as one Metropolitan Government, which is why the Trustee acts as the county's tax collector. On top of real property, the office collects personalty and public utility taxes, runs the state tax relief, tax deferral and tax freeze programs, and handles delinquent taxes, Central Business Improvement District taxes, Gulch district taxes and vegetation liens. The Assessor's office is at 700 President Ronald Reagan Way, Suite 210, Nashville, TN 37210.

  • Tax billing and collection, including payoff questions: 615-862-6330
  • Mortgage inquiries at the Trustee: 615-862-6330
  • Tax relief and tax freeze applications: 615-862-6140
  • Assessor call center for appeal appointments: 615-862-6059

sections.h2: How a Nashville bill is figured
sections.html:
Four pieces make up the math: appraised value, assessment ratio, assessed value and tax rate. The Assessor sets the appraised value. State law fixes the ratio at 25 percent for residential and farm property, 40 percent for commercial and industrial property and 30 percent for personalty.

The Metro Council sets the rate, and it is not final until the State Board of Equalization certifies it. The Trustee shows one rate for the Urban Services District and another for the General Services District, each stated per hundred dollars of assessed value. Your bill shows which district your parcel is in.

Metro Trustee tax rates by service district
Service districtRate per $100 of assessed value
Urban Services District$2.814
General Services District$2.782

To estimate a bill, multiply your appraisal by the ratio, divide by 100, then multiply by the rate for your district. Your appraisal notice and the Trustee's lookup give the real numbers.

sections.h2: When are Nashville property taxes due?
sections.html:
Statements go out in October, and tax must be paid in full by the last day of February to avoid interest. For the bill mailed in October 2026, that deadline is February 28, 2027.

Payment is accepted at the Trustee's office or at a First Horizon Bank financial center, which takes Metro property tax payments from October through February under an arrangement with the Trustee. If a lender escrows your taxes, the servicer normally pays the bill, but the Trustee's mortgage inquiry line can confirm whether a payment posted. Check that before you sign a sale contract, because a missed escrow payment turns into a closing item.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Nashville assessment
sections.html:
Begin with the Assessor and, if that fails, move to the independent Metropolitan Board of Equalization. Informal review closes in the spring, in April, and scheduling a formal appeal closes in late June, so watch the Assessor's site each spring for the exact dates.

The Board of Equalization is created under Metropolitan Charter Article 11, Chapter 2. It has five members appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by the Council, serving two-year terms, and it can send cases to hearing officers. It sits from the first business day of June until that year's equalization is finished. Book through the call center at 615-862-6059.

Bring evidence that supports a lower value as of January 1 of the appeal year:

  • Comparable sales close to your home in age, features and square footage, with size within about 20 percent of yours
  • Any fee appraisal you already hold, which the board treats as an opinion to review and not an automatic answer
  • Repair estimates for needed work, not routine upkeep
  • Photographs of damage or outdated kitchens and baths

A relative may file for the owner. Anyone else, including an attorney or tax representative, needs a signed letter of authorization that names the parcel and the assessment year. If the board's decision disappoints you, you have 45 days after the board mails its notice to go to the State Board of Equalization.

Homeowners aged 65 and up, disabled homeowners, disabled veteran owners and surviving spouses of disabled veteran owners can apply for state-funded tax relief through the Trustee. The program dates to a 1973 constitutional amendment, and Metro adopted it locally.

For the current window the Trustee lists an income cap of $38,470 for Davidson County, measured on 2025 income for all owners and a spouse. Applicants must have turned 65 by December 31 of the tax year, show the home is their principal residence, and sign a form that lets the Trustee check income with the IRS, Social Security or the state. Applications run through April 5, 2027. Anyone already enrolled in the relief or freeze programs must return a voucher by April 5 every year to stay in. Call 615-862-6140 before you gather paperwork, because the veteran and spouse routes use separate forms.

sections.h2: What happens when Nashville property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
After the last day of February, the bill is delinquent and interest applies under Tennessee law. The Trustee's office handles delinquent taxes, so that is where you ask for a payoff figure with interest counted through a specific closing date.

Liens matter to a seller too. The Trustee collects vegetation liens and the special district taxes mentioned above, so ask whether any of them sit on your parcel. A title company will search for all of them. Pulling an account history from the Trustee early keeps a surprise charge from delaying closing.

sections.h2: Selling a Nashville house with tax still owed
sections.html:
You can sell it. Unpaid property tax is cleared from the sale money at closing, and the title company asks the Trustee for the exact amount.

  • Call 615-862-6330 and ask for the balance, interest and any lien lines on your parcel.
  • Tell the closing agent the date you expect to close so interest is counted to that day.
  • If the house is vacant or inherited, confirm who the Trustee has on file to receive the bill, since a statement mailed to a former owner is easy to miss.
  • Compare any offer with the amount owed, because a low price can leave you short of the tax and loan balances.

Owners facing a large tax balance often weigh a sale to a buyer who closes as-is, which saves repair costs and showing time. Whatever route you choose, get the payoff in writing from the Trustee before you accept terms.

Davidson County had 745,904 residents in the July 2025 estimate, a 4.2 percent rise over the 2020 base, with 389,379 housing units and 324,907 households for 2020 to 2024. Owners occupy 52.8 percent of homes, so close to half of households rent. The median owner-occupied value is $417,400 and median gross rent is $1,582.

faqs.q: Is there a separate Nashville city tax on top of the county tax?
faqs.a: No. Nashville and Davidson County are one government, with one rate per service district: $2.814 in the Urban Services District and $2.782 in the General Services District, each per hundred dollars of assessed value. Your bill shows which applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: By what date must 2026 Nashville property tax be paid to avoid interest?
faqs.a: The last day of February 2027, which is February 28. The Trustee mails statements in October.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Nashville property value?
faqs.a: Informal review with the Assessor closes in the spring, and scheduling a formal Board of Equalization appeal closes in late June. After a board hearing, the state board accepts an appeal for 45 days after the notice is mailed.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for Nashville property tax relief?
faqs.a: Owners aged 65 and up, disabled owners, disabled veteran owners and their surviving spouses, if they meet the income limit. The Trustee lists $38,470 for Davidson County based on 2025 income, and applications are open through April 5, 2027.

faqs.q: Who do I call to find out what I owe before closing?
faqs.a: Call the Metropolitan Trustee's tax billing and collection line at 615-862-6330 and ask for a payoff that includes interest to your expected closing date. Give the same figure to your title company so the balance comes out of your proceeds.
